observation_summary: The intersection() method in both 2D and 3D SubLine classes fails to check if the intersection of the underlying lines is null before passing that result to toSubSpace(), leading to a NullPointerException when lines are parallel or non-intersecting.
hypothesis: The intersection() method in SubLine (both 2D and 3D) calls line.intersection(subLine.line) which returns null for parallel or non-intersecting lines. This null result is then passed directly to line.toSubSpace(v), causing a NullPointerException when the code attempts to use the null vector.
prediction: The intersection() method will show that the result of line.intersection() is not checked for null before being passed to toSubSpace().
experiment_rationale: The stack trace and source code clearly show that the intersection point (v1D or v2D) is calculated and immediately used in a method call (toSubSpace) without any null check, despite the fact that the underlying line intersection method is documented to return null for non-intersecting lines.
reasoning_summary: The code in SubLine.intersection() (both 2D and 3D) performs a call to line.intersection() and immediately uses the result in a method call (toSubSpace) without verifying if the result is null. This is a classic missing guard condition.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The logic for calculating the intersection is correct; the issue is the failure to handle the 'no intersection' case (null) before proceeding.
